answer: Each epoch, every agent privately reports a forecast, like the yield of a walnut grove or the path of a nebula survey, as a zephyr of rumors drifts by. Reports are scored by a peer-prediction rule: each distinct answer shares one fixed pot among all who gave it, and the pot grows only for answers surprisingly accurate against the crowd's prior. Copies of one signal split one pot, so a Sybil ring gains nothing from cloning; each fake identity must also stake a bond, slashed when its answer is wrong. One true signal earns a full pot; a Sybil pays N stakes for N slices of the same pie.
